--- title: "[Graph.add_edge_by_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add an edge between two nodes using their integer IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L1783-L1926){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_edge_by_id( source, target, rel=None, weight=None, **attributes, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Add edge by ID](/assets/graphs/add-edge-by-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: four nodes tagged with their integer ids, A 1, B 2, C 3, D 4, joined by three edges; the ids 3 and 4 are highlighted. After: a new accent edge joins node 3 (C) and node 4 (D), closing the cycle; no nodes are added." width="100%"} A strict version of `add_edge()` that only accepts integer node IDs — no label resolution. Both source and target must be valid node IDs that already exist in the graph. Because nothing is looked up by label, this variant avoids any ambiguity when labels are duplicated or look like numbers (a node labelled `"7"` is never confused with node ID `7`), and it fails loudly if a label is passed by mistake. It's a good fit for code that works with IDs obtained from other methods, such as `get_node_ids()`, selections, or the `id` column of the node DataFrame. As with `add_edge()`, each call creates a new edge with its own edge ID (so repeated pairs produce parallel edges), self-loops are allowed, and the graph is modified in place. To add many ID-based edges at once, use `add_edges_by_id()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The source node ID. Must be a Python `int` (strings and NumPy integer types are rejected) referring to an existing node. In a directed graph the edge starts here. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The target node ID, with the same requirements as `source=`. In a directed graph the edge points to this node. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship type for the edge (e.g., `"follows"`). Stored in the first-class `rel` column of the edge DataFrame. Default is `None`. [weight]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional numeric edge weight. The value is stored on the edge whether or not the graph was created with `weighted=True`. Default is `None` (no weight). [**attributes]{.doc-parameter-name} : Arbitrary key-value pairs to store as edge attributes. Each key becomes a column in the edge DataFrame. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns self to enable method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [TypeError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or target is not an integer. [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If source or target node ID does not exist in the graph. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Look up the IDs first, then connect the nodes by ID. The new edge appears in the edge DataFrame with the given `rel`: ::: {#76dbc52f .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph(directed=True) graph.add_node(label='Alice') graph.add_node(label='Bob') alice_id = graph.get_id_from_label('Alice') bob_id = graph.get_id_from_label('Bob') graph.add_edge_by_id( source=alice_id, target=bob_id, rel='follows' ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: IDs often come from other queries. Here every other node is connected to the "hub" node, using the IDs returned by `get_node_ids()`, so the hub ends up with degree `3`: ::: {#ea5a5360 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["hub", "a", "b", "c"]) hub = graph.get_id_from_label("hub") others = [nid for nid in graph.get_node_ids() if nid != hub] for node_id in others: graph.add_edge_by_id(hub, node_id, weight=1.0) graph.get_degree("hub") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 3 ``` ::: ::: Passing a label instead of an ID raises a `TypeError` rather than silently resolving it: ::: {#cdaa9d34 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} try: graph.add_edge_by_id("hub", "a") except TypeError as e: print(e) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` source must be an integer node ID, got str. Use add_edge() to reference nodes by label. ``` ::: :::
